title: A Windows clone works end to end
goal: A Windows 11 clone with Git for Windows works end to end and CI proves it: revision reads survive long Windows paths, the raw-read hint fires under the PowerShell tool, the tests compile without warnings, a run of tests.py on the Windows host by a Claude session is on record for each change to the tools, the session-end launcher is proven on Windows, and a clean host has gone from no Python to a passing /kb-setup on record.
notes: Setup from no Python (install-python.ps1, uv pin, PowerShell allow rules, the missing-interpreter notice) landed with sprint SP-fep4fpsx “Windows ready”; the suite's Windows failures with BG-ovulgaal. Clauses met: the raw-read hint under PowerShell (.claude/settings.json PowerShell matcher, SP-hlfwfcx6; kb_hook.raw_read_nudge prints a hint on a planted Get-Content event), the tests compile without warnings (compileall -W error over _tools passes; a guard is a story). Later, not yet a story: a tool that ties kb/_self/reports/windows-run.md's recorded commit to the _tools/ changes since (nothing reads it now); a green kb-tests-windows run on main under the all-manual CI jobs; the signed-in half of the clean host (sign-in, kb_mcp.py --register-local, MCP calls), which needs a Claude Code sign-in on a throwaway account. Out of scope, host setup rather than repository changes: running kbgit.py install-hooks and kb_mcp.py --register-local in a clone (/kb-setup does), a remote layout, turning off the Store's App Execution Aliases, enabling LongPathsEnabled, running Claude Code unelevated.
